title: Animals And Birds Their State Of Invocation And The Introduction To 3 Truths

questions.question: What new group did the traveler come to after moving ahead on his thinking journey?
questions.answer: The world of animals and birds.

questions.question: How was the traveler feeling as he went on?
questions.answer: He was more eager and full of faith and understanding.

questions.question: What opened in front of his mind?
questions.answer: A door to the animal and bird world.

questions.question: How was he invited to come in?
questions.answer: By many different voices and ways of speaking.

questions.question: What were the animals and birds saying by their state and sounds?
questions.answer: That Allah is One.

questions.question: What did they turn the earth into?
questions.answer: A huge place of remembering and praising Allah.

questions.question: What was each animal and bird like?
questions.answer: Like a sign, a message, and a thankful praise to Allah.

questions.question: What did each one show about Allah?
questions.answer: His mercy and His making.

questions.question: What parts of animals and birds seemed like neat words or good sentences?
questions.answer: Their senses, powers, body parts, and tools.

questions.question: How many big truths did the traveler notice in them?
questions.answer: Three.

questions.question: What does the first truth say about how animals were made?
questions.answer: They were made with wisdom, purpose, and care, not by chance.

questions.question: What things could not be the maker of animals, according to the first truth?
questions.answer: Luck, blind power, or lifeless nature.

questions.question: What does the first truth show about Allah?
questions.answer: That He is ever-living, self-sustaining, and One.

questions.question: What does the second truth notice about animals?
questions.answer: They are different from each other and beautifully shaped.

questions.question: Why does the second truth say only Allah could do this?
questions.answer: Because it takes complete power and knowledge to make so many wonderful kinds.

questions.question: Who is traveling and thinking in this passage?
questions.answer: A traveler who is looking at creation carefully.

questions.question: What gift did he carry in his heart and mind as he continued?
questions.answer: More faith and understanding.

questions.question: Which living things did he study in this part?
questions.answer: Animals and birds.

questions.question: Did he hear only one voice inviting him, or many?
questions.answer: Many voices.

questions.question: What did he see all kinds of animals and birds doing together?
questions.answer: Declaring that Allah alone is worthy of worship.

questions.question: In the passage, did they do this only with sound?
questions.answer: No. Some did it quietly and some with sound.

questions.question: What happened to the face of the earth because of them?
questions.answer: It became like a big place of prayer and praise.

questions.question: Each animal was compared to what kinds of things?
questions.answer: A poem, a word of praise, and a letter pointing to mercy.

questions.question: Besides praising Allah, what else was each creature doing?
questions.answer: Telling about its Maker and thanking Him.

questions.question: What looked orderly and balanced in the animals and birds?
questions.answer: Their senses, abilities, limbs, and other parts.

questions.question: What did the traveler learn from these well-made parts?
questions.answer: That they thank their Creator and point to His oneness.

questions.question: What is one reason the first truth is strong?
questions.answer: Living things are made skillfully and on purpose.

questions.question: Why is “made by chance” rejected in the first truth?
questions.answer: Because living things show knowledge, wisdom, and will.

questions.question: What does the second truth focus on more: sameness only or careful differences?
questions.answer: Careful differences.

questions.question: Give one example of these careful differences.
questions.answer: Their features, shapes, sizes, or beautiful forms.

questions.question: What realm opened to the traveler’s understanding?
questions.answer: The realm of animals and birds.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the traveler—was he ignoring creation or studying it?
questions.answer: He was studying it carefully.

questions.question: What showed that there were very many creatures in that realm?
questions.answer: There were countless voices and many different groups and kinds.

questions.question: What message were all those creatures giving?
questions.answer: That Allah is One.

questions.question: How widely did this message spread on earth?
questions.answer: Across the whole earth.

questions.question: What was the earth compared to because of their praise?
questions.answer: A giant gathering place for remembering and glorifying Allah.

questions.question: How was each creature like writing or speech?
questions.answer: It was like a poem, a word, or a letter.

questions.question: What did these living “messages” point to?
questions.answer: Allah’s mercy and His making.

questions.question: What body features seemed like clear, orderly speech?
questions.answer: Their senses, strengths, limbs, and tools.

questions.question: What two big things did the three truths prove?
questions.answer: That creatures thank their Creator and show His oneness.

questions.question: In the first truth, what kind of making is described?
questions.answer: Wise, purposeful, and skillful making.

questions.question: What does being alive in such a careful way show?
questions.answer: It shows knowledge, wisdom, and will.

questions.question: About how many creatures repeat this witness in the first truth?
questions.answer: As many as all living creatures.

questions.question: In the second truth, what stands out when we look at many animals?
questions.answer: Their different looks and their beautiful, measured forms.

questions.question: Why can’t just anything make such creatures?
questions.answer: Because making them needs complete power and complete knowledge.

questions.question: As the traveler moved forward, what increased inside him?
questions.answer: His eagerness, faith, and understanding.

questions.question: What season was used to help describe what he had gathered?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: What living world came next for him to look at?
questions.answer: The world of animals and birds.

questions.question: How did that world call him in?
questions.answer: With many voices and many kinds of expression.

questions.question: What did he notice about the many species and groups?
questions.answer: They were all giving one message about Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What did their praising do to the earth?
questions.answer: It made the earth like a huge place of worship and praise.

questions.question: What three comparisons are used for each creature?
questions.answer: A poem, a praising word, and a letter.

questions.question: What did each creature describe besides giving praise?
questions.answer: Its Maker.

questions.question: Which parts of the creatures looked carefully arranged?
questions.answer: Their senses, powers, members, and instruments.

questions.question: What did this careful arrangement help prove?
questions.answer: That they were thanking their Creator and showing His unity.

questions.question: What is the first of the three truths mainly about?
questions.answer: That living things are made with wisdom and purpose.

questions.question: What false ideas are pushed away by the first truth?
questions.answer: Chance, blind force, and lifeless nature.

questions.question: What is the second truth mainly about?
questions.answer: The special differences and beauty in creatures.

questions.question: What do measured proportions and nice forms tell us?
questions.answer: They tell us the Maker is wise, powerful, and knowing.

questions.question: What kind of journey is the traveler on in this passage?
questions.answer: A thinking journey through creation.

questions.question: What opened to his understanding during this journey?
questions.answer: The gate to animals and birds.

questions.question: Who welcomed him into that gate?
questions.answer: Animals and birds with many voices.

questions.question: What was the big message shared by all their kinds?
questions.answer: That there is only one true God, Allah.

questions.question: What did the whole earth become because of their message?
questions.answer: A broad place of calling on and glorifying Allah.

questions.question: How is one animal or bird described in a special way?
questions.answer: As a beautiful sign of praise and thanks.

questions.question: What did each one point to about Allah?
questions.answer: His mercy.

questions.question: What did each one tell about Allah?
questions.answer: That He is the Maker.

questions.question: What in the creatures looked like disciplined speech?
questions.answer: Their abilities and body parts.

questions.question: How many major truths did the traveler see in them?
questions.answer: Three.

questions.question: What does the first truth teach about the start of animal life?
questions.answer: It begins by Allah’s wise and purposeful making.

questions.question: Why is random luck not a good answer for animal life in this passage?
questions.answer: Because animals show skill, order, wisdom, and will.

questions.question: What does the first truth say life displays many times over?
questions.answer: Knowledge, wisdom, and will.

questions.question: What does the second truth notice about the creatures’ outward appearance?
questions.answer: Their looks are distinct, decorated, balanced, and orderly.

questions.question: What does that outward beauty help us infer about the Maker?
questions.answer: He has full power and full knowledge.

questions.question: What was the traveler using on his journey besides his eyes?
questions.answer: His mind and understanding.

questions.question: What was placed before his understanding in this passage?
questions.answer: An opening to the animal and bird world.

questions.question: Were the invitations into that world few or many?
questions.answer: Many.

questions.question: What did he realize all animal and bird groups were announcing?
questions.answer: Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does it mean that some creatures proclaimed this silently?
questions.answer: Their very state and design showed it even without words.

questions.question: What was the earth turned into by their praising?
questions.answer: A very large gathering place for worship and glorification.

questions.question: What is one way each creature was like a message?
questions.answer: It pointed to Allah and thanked Him.

questions.question: What did the traveler think about the animals’ senses and limbs?
questions.answer: They were arranged like orderly and meaningful words.

questions.question: What two things were the creatures doing in a clear way?
questions.answer: Thanking their Creator and testifying to His unity.

questions.question: What kind of creation is described in the first truth?
questions.answer: Creation with wisdom, purpose, and skill.

questions.question: What three wrong explanations are rejected there?
questions.answer: Chance, blind force, and lifeless nature.

questions.question: What names or qualities of Allah are shown in the first truth?
questions.answer: That He is living, self-sustaining, and One.

questions.question: What does the second truth say about the creatures’ differences?
questions.answer: Their differences are carefully chosen and beautifully made.

questions.question: What details in the second truth show order?
questions.answer: Their features, shapes, sizes, and forms fit together well.

questions.question: Why is the work in the second truth too great for anyone but Allah?
questions.answer: Because it includes endless wisdom and wonders in every way.
